- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >2.00), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 15–25% for 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and price is stable, model underestimates; increase forecast by 5–15% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or low; add 5–10% bias upward for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model tends to overcorrect after recent spikes; apply mean reversion adjustment: if forecast > 1.5× recent 7-day average, reduce by 20–40%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 10–20% for 5–10 day horizon to compensate for low sentiment bias.
